source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Locomotion and Reproduction in Protozoa
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: On the basis of locomotor organelles, Amoeba, Euglena, Paramecium and Plasmodium represent
options: sarcodine, flagellate, ciliate and sporozoan types
questions.explanation: Sarcodina use pseudopodia, Mastigophora flagella, Ciliata cilia; Sporozoa (Apicomplexa) lack locomotor organelles in the adult.

questions.stem: Lobe-like pseudopodia of Amoeba used in creeping are called
questions.explanation: Amoeba has blunt lobopodia; foraminiferans have reticulopodia and heliozoans have axopodia.

questions.stem: Euglena swims mainly by the beat of its
questions.explanation: A long locomotory flagellum emerges from the anterior reservoir; a shorter flagellum is within it.

questions.stem: Paramecium moves rapidly by coordinated beating of
questions.explanation: The pellicle bears thousands of cilia whose metachronal waves push the cell through water.

questions.stem: The wriggling change of body shape in Euglena without using flagella is
questions.explanation: Myonemes under the pellicle produce metaboly, a peristaltic change of form.

questions.stem: Amoeba typically divides into two daughters by
options: longitudinal binary fission of the whole cell
questions.explanation: Amoeba shows simple (irregular) binary fission; the plane is not fixed as in flagellates or ciliates.

questions.stem: Schizogony in Plasmodium is a form of
options: binary fission in the mosquito gut
questions.explanation: The nucleus divides repeatedly and the cytoplasm splits into many merozoites (schizonts) in liver and RBC.

questions.stem: Temporary fusion of two Paramecium individuals for nuclear exchange is called
questions.explanation: Conjugation is a sexual process: micronuclei undergo meiosis and a migratory pronucleus is exchanged.

questions.stem: Fusion of similar-sized gametes in protozoa is termed
questions.explanation: Isogamy: gametes alike in size; anisogamy: unlike sizes; oogamy: large ovum and small sperm.

questions.stem: When conditions are unfavourable, Amoeba often survives by
questions.explanation: Encystment walls off the cell; excystment and binary fission resume when moisture and food return.

questions.stem: Binary fission in Euglena is typically
options: longitudinal, beginning at the anterior end
multiple, producing eight cells at once
questions.explanation: Flagellates divide along the long axis; ciliates such as Paramecium divide transversely.

questions.stem: Reticulopodia that anastomose into a network occur in
questions.explanation: Foraminiferan rhizopods put out branching, fusing filose threads (reticulopodia) through shell pores.

questions.stem: Which statement about protozoan reproduction is incorrect?
options: Paramecium conjugation restores a new macronucleus after meiosis of micronuclei
Plasmodium sporogony in the mosquito is a sexual cycle ending in sporozoites
Multiple fission of a Plasmodium schizont is asexual
Adult Plasmodium in RBC swims by a pair of flagella
questions.explanation: Malaria parasites in blood lack flagella; only microgametes in the mosquito are flagellated.

questions.stem: Which protozoan lacks specialised locomotor organelles in the trophic adult?
questions.explanation: Sporozoans are typically non-motile as adults; an amoeba, euglena and paramecium use pseudopodia, flagella and cilia.

questions.stem: Axopodia with a stiff axial filament are characteristic of
questions.explanation: Axopodia are slender, needle-like pseudopodia supported by a microtubular axoneme.

questions.stem: The photoreceptive stigma (eyespot) that orients swimming in light occurs in
questions.explanation: Euglena has a red stigma near the reservoir that shades a photo-sensitive swelling of the flagellum.

questions.stem: Avoiding reaction in Paramecium, in which ciliary beat reverses, is triggered when the cell
options: encounters an obstacle or harmful stimulus at the anterior end
questions.explanation: Reversal of ciliary effective stroke backs the cell away, then it swivels and moves off in a new direction.

questions.stem: Metabolic movement depends on contractile myonemes in the pellicle of
questions.explanation: Euglenoid movement is a change of body outline produced by pellicular myonemes, distinct from flagellar swimming.

questions.stem: Transverse binary fission is the usual asexual method in
questions.explanation: Ciliates divide across the short axis so each daughter keeps rows of cilia; flagellates divide lengthwise.

questions.stem: Sporogony of Plasmodium, producing sporozoites, takes place in the
options: mosquito, on the outer wall of the midgut and then in salivary glands
questions.explanation: After zygote formation, the oocyst on the mosquito gut wall yields sporozoites that invade salivary glands.

questions.stem: During conjugation, the macronucleus of Paramecium
options: disintegrates and is later reformed from a micronuclear product
questions.explanation: The vegetative macronucleus breaks down; a new one is differentiated after fusion of pronuclei.

questions.stem: Oogamy in protozoa refers to fusion of
options: a large non-motile female gamete and a small motile male gamete
questions.explanation: Oogamy is the extreme of anisogamy, as in Plasmodium (macrogamete + microgamete) in the mosquito.

questions.stem: The infective stage of Plasmodium injected into humans by the mosquito is the
questions.explanation: Sporozoites from salivary glands enter blood, then liver; merozoites later invade erythrocytes.

questions.stem: Sol-gel theory of amoeboid movement proposes that
options: ectoplasm gelates at the advancing tip while plasmasol flows forward
the pellicle is rigid and never changes
questions.explanation: Endoplasm (plasmasol) streams into a new pseudopodium as peripheral ectoplasm (plasmagel) forms and later solates at the rear.

questions.stem: Which comparison of binary fission is correct?
questions.explanation: Flagellates split along the long axis; ciliates across it; amoebae divide without a fixed plane.

questions.stem: Select the incorrect statement about protozoan motility and reproduction.
options: Hologamy is fusion of two fully grown individuals acting as gametes
Conjugation in Paramecium involves meiosis of the micronucleus
Plasmodium exhibits both schizogony and sporogony in its life cycle
Cilia of Paramecium are structurally unrelated to the flagellum of Euglena
questions.explanation: Cilia and flagella share the 9+2 microtubule axoneme; they differ mainly in number, length and beat pattern.
